title_en: Measures for the Implementation of the Law of the People's Republic of China on the Protection of Military Installations

articles.content_en: Article 1 These Measures are formulated in accordance with the provisions of the Law of the People's Republic of China on the Protection of Military Facilities (hereinafter referred to as the Military Facilities Protection Law).

Article 2 In places where military facilities are located, the local people's government at or above the county level and the relevant military organs stationed there shall jointly establish a military facilities protection committee, which shall be responsible for coordinating and guiding the protection of military facilities within its administrative area.
The office of the military facilities protection committee shall be established in the provincial military command (garrison command, garrison district), military sub-command (garrison district), or the people's armed forces department of the county (autonomous county, city, or municipal district), and shall handle the day-to-day work of the military facilities protection committee.

Article 4 The General Staff Headquarters of the People's Liberation Army, under the leadership of the State Council and the Central Military Commission, shall take charge of the protection of military facilities nationwide and guide the work of military facilities protection committees at all levels.
The command organ of a military command shall take charge of the protection of military facilities within its jurisdiction and guide the work of military facilities protection committees at all levels within its jurisdiction.
A military facilities protection committee at a higher level shall guide the work of a military facilities protection committee at a lower level.

Article 5 The relevant departments of the State Council shall, within their respective functions and duties, be responsible for the relevant work concerning the protection of military facilities and assist the military organs in implementing the measures for the protection of military facilities.
The local people's governments at or above the county level shall be responsible for the relevant work concerning the protection of military facilities within their administrative areas and assist the military organs stationed there in implementing the measures for the protection of military facilities.

Article 6 The military organs shall introduce to the local people's government the relevant information concerning the military facilities and solicit the opinions of the local people's government; the local people's government shall introduce to the military organs stationed there the relevant information concerning economic development and solicit the opinions of the military organs stationed there.

Article 7 People's governments and military organs at all levels shall commend and reward organizations and individuals that have made outstanding achievements in the protection of military facilities.

Article 8 The determination and delimitation of military restricted zones and military administrative zones, as well as the delimitation of safety control zones outside military restricted zones, shall be handled in accordance with the Military Facilities Protection Law and the relevant provisions of the State Council and the Central Military Commission.

Article 9 In a military restricted zone on waters, non-military vessels shall be prohibited from entering, and it shall be prohibited to construct or install non-military facilities, to engage in aquaculture, fishing, or other activities that obstruct the operations, security, and confidentiality of military vessels.

Article 10 In a military administrative zone on waters, it shall be prohibited to construct or install non-military facilities, and to engage in aquaculture; engaging in fishing or other activities shall not affect the operations of military vessels.

Article 11 In the waters of a port jointly used by military and civilian authorities that is designated as a military administrative zone, separate management by the military and local authorities shall be implemented; if a non-military facility needs to be newly constructed within the waters under local management, consent from the relevant military facility management unit shall be obtained in advance.

Article 12 Signboards shall be erected in military restricted zones and military administrative zones. The form, material, and specifications of the signboards shall be prescribed by the military facilities protection committee of the province, autonomous region, or municipality directly under the Central Government, and the signboards shall be erected by the local people's government at or above the county level.
Where it is difficult to set boundary markers or obstacles to indicate the extent of a military restricted zone or military administrative zone on waters in the actual waters, the local competent departments of transportation and fisheries shall jointly announce the extent to the public, and the competent department of surveying and mapping shall mark it on the nautical charts.

Article 13 The term "combat engineering" as used in the Military Facilities Protection Law includes tunnels, permanent fortifications, and supporting special-purpose roads, bridges and culverts, as well as ancillary facilities such as water sources, power supply, and war reserve rooms.

Article 14 For combat engineering not included in military restricted zones or military administrative zones, a safety protection scope shall be delimited outside the combat engineering. The safety protection scope of combat engineering shall be proposed by the provincial military command or the superior military organ at or above the army level that manages the combat engineering, based on the deployment of the engineering, the terrain, and the local economic development, and shall be submitted to the military region and the people's government of the province, autonomous region, or municipality directly under the Central Government for approval.
In areas where combat engineering is relatively concentrated, the safety protection scopes of combat engineering may be delimited in contiguous tracts.

Article 15 The delimitation of the safety protection scope of combat engineering shall not affect the ownership or right to use of the land and its attachments within the safety protection scope. Units and residents within the safety protection scope may continue their production and daily life as normal, but shall not endanger the security, confidentiality, and functional effectiveness of the military facilities.

Article 16 Within the safety protection scope of combat engineering, it shall be prohibited to quarry, mine, blast, or fell trees; the construction of buildings, structures, roads, and the carrying out of capital construction on farmland and water conservancy shall obtain the consent of the superior military organ in charge of the combat engineering management unit and the local military facilities protection committee, and shall not affect the security, confidentiality, and functional effectiveness of the combat engineering.

Article 17 It shall be prohibited to open a sealed combat engineering without authorization, to destroy the camouflage of combat engineering, or to block the access passages to and from combat engineering.
Without the approval of the superior military organ at or above the division level that manages the combat engineering, it shall not be permitted to photograph, videotape, survey, measure, describe, or record the combat engineering, or to store non-military materials or equipment in the combat engineering, or to engage in production activities such as planting or breeding.

Article 18 If a new project or construction project cannot practically avoid combat engineering, an application for demolishing, relocating, or altering the combat engineering shall be submitted in accordance with the relevant state provisions; without the approval of the application, the combat engineering shall not be demolished, relocated, or altered.

Article 19 The term "clearance of military airfields" as used in these Measures refers to the spatial area around the flight field that is delimited to restrict the height of objects in order to ensure the safety of takeoff, landing, and go-around of military aircraft (including helicopters).
The standards for the protection of clearance of military airfields shall be implemented in accordance with the relevant state provisions.
Article 20 Within the clearance protection area of a military airfield, it shall be prohibited to construct buildings, structures, or other facilities that exceed the airfield clearance standards.

Article 21 Within the clearance protection area of a military airport, planting vegetation, setting up lights or objects, discharging smoke, dust, flames, exhaust gases, or engaging in other similar activities shall not affect flight safety or the operational efficiency of airport navigation aids.

Article 22 The management unit of a military airport shall be informed of local urban planning, village and town planning, and plans for the construction of tall buildings, and shall provide technical consultation on the clearance protection of the military airport.

Article 23 Where a construction unit intends to construct tall buildings, structures, or other facilities within the clearance protection area of a military airport, it must, before applying for project approval, seek in writing the opinions of the military authority at or above the corps level that is the competent authority of the management unit of the military airport; where the opinions of the military authority have not been sought, or the designed height of the construction project exceeds the clearance protection standards of the military airport, the relevant departments of the State Council and the relevant departments of the local people's government shall not handle the construction permit procedures.

Article 24 The management unit of a military airport shall periodically inspect the clearance protection situation of the airport, and upon discovering that buildings, structures, or other facilities exceeding the clearance protection standards of the military airport have been constructed without authorization, shall promptly report to its superior and the local military facilities protection committee.
The local people's government shall be informed of the relevant clearance protection situation of the local military airport, formulate protection measures, and urge relevant entities to install flight obstruction markings on tall buildings, structures, or other facilities within the clearance protection area of the military airport.

Article 25 Where tall buildings, structures, or other facilities are newly constructed near existing natural obstacles within the lateral clearance protection area of a military airport, the construction must comply with the relevant state provisions on airport clearance.

Article 26 The clearance protection work for military-civilian airports and for retained old airports and highway runways managed by the military shall be governed by the relevant provisions on clearance protection of military airports.

Article 28 For the purposes of the Law on the Protection of Military Facilities, military oil and water pipelines refer to surface, underground, or underwater oil and water pipelines exclusively used by the military, as well as pressurization stations, metering stations, treatment yards, oil depots, valve chambers, markers, and other ancillary facilities along the pipelines.

Article 29 The management units of military communication and power transmission lines and military oil and water pipelines (hereinafter referred to as military pipelines) shall strengthen maintenance and management work, adhere to the system of patrol and testing inspections; when necessary, they may organize armed patrols, and shall promptly handle any problems discovered.

Article 30 The local people's governments at all levels and the stationed military authorities shall, according to the actual circumstances, organize the masses along the military pipelines to implement joint military-civilian pipeline protection, adopting forms such as entrusted guarding and sectional responsibility, to protect the safety of the military pipelines.

Article 31 Underground military pipelines shall have route markers or permanent signs installed, and sections (parts) prone to damage shall have signboards set up. Underwater military pipelines shall be marked on nautical charts.

Article 32 The specific protection requirements for military pipelines and the handling of mutual interference between military pipelines and other facilities shall be carried out in accordance with the relevant provisions of the State Council and the Central Military Commission.

Article 33 For the purposes of these Measures, the term "electromagnetic environment of military fixed radio facilities" (hereinafter referred to as military electromagnetic environment) means the area delineated around military fixed facilities such as radio receiving (transmitting) stations, reconnaissance, direction finding, radar, navigation and positioning stations to ensure their normal operation, within which electromagnetic interference signals and electromagnetic obstruction objects are restricted.
The specific protection requirements for the military electromagnetic environment shall be implemented in accordance with the relevant standards prescribed by the State.

Article 34 Within the protected scope of the military electromagnetic environment, no equipment that emits or radiates electromagnetic signals or electromagnetic obstruction objects shall be constructed, installed, or used.

Article 35 Where local authorities arrange construction projects within the protected scope of the military electromagnetic environment that may affect the military electromagnetic environment, they shall, in accordance with the provisions, seek the opinions of the relevant military authorities; when necessary, the military facility management unit and the relevant local departments may jointly test and evaluate the degree of interference and the impact of electromagnetic obstruction objects.

Article 36 The relevant departments of the people's governments at all levels, when approving and accepting construction projects within the protected scope of the military electromagnetic environment, shall review the status of equipment that emits or radiates electromagnetic signals and electromagnetic obstruction objects, as well as the situation of having sought opinions from the military authorities; where the opinions of the military authorities have not been sought, or the project does not meet the national electromagnetic environment protection standards, they shall not handle the construction or use permit procedures.

Article 37 The management unit of military fixed radio facilities shall be informed of the protection situation of the military electromagnetic environment, and upon discovering any problems, shall promptly report to its superior military authority and the local military facilities protection committee.

Article 38 For the purposes of these Measures, border defense facilities refer to military facilities used and managed by border defense troops, such as border patrol roads, border barbed wire fences (iron fences), border monitoring equipment, auxiliary border management signs, border helicopter landing pads, and border vessel berthing points.
Article 39 No organization or individual shall, without the consent of the management unit of the border defense facilities, dismantle or move the border defense facilities without authorization.

Article 40 Where projects such as opening ports, border trade zones, tourist attractions, or constructing roads, pipelines, bridges in border areas involve border defense facilities, the opinions of the military authorities shall be sought in accordance with the relevant provisions; where border defense facilities need to be relocated or modified, approval shall be obtained from the military facilities protection committee of the relevant province, autonomous region, or municipality directly under the Central Government; the location, quality, and standards of the relocated or modified border defense facilities must comply with the relevant state provisions.
Article 41 The protection of military surveying markers shall be handled in accordance with the provisions of relevant national laws and regulations.

Article 43 Violating the provisions of Article 9, Article 10 and Article 11 of these Measures, where anyone constructs or sets up non-military facilities within a water area military restricted zone, a water area military administrative zone or the water area of a military-civilian port, the administrative departments of urban planning, transportation and fishery shall, in accordance with their respective functions and powers, order the cessation of the construction activities; if already constructed, order removal within a prescribed time limit.

Article 44 Violating the provisions of Article 9 and Article 10 of these Measures, where anyone enters a water area military restricted zone without authorization, engages in aquaculture or fishing within a water area military restricted zone, or engages in aquaculture within a water area military administrative zone, the administrative departments of transportation and fishery shall, in accordance with their respective functions and powers, give a warning, order to leave, and may confiscate fishing gear and catches.

Article 45 Violating the provisions of Article 16 of these Measures, where anyone quarries, mines, blasts, or fells trees within the safety protection area of combat engineering works, the public security organ and the administrative departments of land and resources and forestry shall, in accordance with their respective functions and powers, order cessation of the illegal act, confiscate the extracted products and illegal gains; if losses are caused, compensation for the losses shall be made according to law.

Article 46 Violating the provisions of Article 16 of these Measures, where anyone without authorization constructs buildings, structures or roads or carries out farmland water conservancy capital construction within the safety protection area of combat engineering works, the administrative departments of urban planning, transportation and agriculture shall, in accordance with their respective functions and powers, give a warning and order rectification within a prescribed time limit; if losses are caused, compensation for the losses shall be made according to law.

Article 47 Violating the provisions of Article 17 of these Measures, where anyone damages the closed camouflage of combat engineering works, blocks the passages of combat engineering works, or uses the combat engineering works for stacking goods, planting or breeding, the public security organ shall order cessation of the illegal act and restoration of the original condition within a prescribed time limit; if losses are caused, compensation for the losses shall be made according to law.

Article 48 Violating the provisions of Article 20 and Article 25 of these Measures, where anyone constructs buildings, structures or other facilities exceeding the clearance protection standards of a military airport within the clearance protection area of the military airport, the administrative department of urban planning shall order removal of the parts exceeding the height limit within a prescribed time limit.

Article 49 Violating the provisions of Article 34 of these Measures, where anyone constructs, sets up or uses equipment that emits or radiates electromagnetic signals and electromagnetic obstructing objects within a military electromagnetic environment protection area, the administrative departments of urban planning and information industry shall, in accordance with their respective functions and powers, give a warning and order rectification within a prescribed time limit; if they refuse to rectify, seal up the interfering equipment or forcibly remove the obstacles.

Article 50 Violating the provisions of Article 18, Article 39 and Article 40 of these Measures, where anyone without authorization demolishes, relocates or alters combat engineering works or border defense facilities, or without authorization moves border defense facilities, the administrative department of urban planning shall order cessation of the illegal act and restoration of the original condition within a prescribed time limit; if losses are caused, compensation for the losses shall be made according to law.

Article 51 Violating these Measures, if the act constitutes a violation of public security administration, the public security organ shall impose a punishment according to law; if a crime is constituted, criminal liability shall be investigated according to law.
Article 52 The protection of the military installations belonging to the Chinese People's Armed Police Force shall be governed by the Military Installations Protection Law and these Measures.
Article 53 These Measures shall come into force as of the date of promulgation.
